html:
SMTO-SKL-0143 — SMTO doesn't know if your Slack change went through

GUID: fdb23f76-0fd5-5064-b3e0-73c7ff1bde95
Slug: slack-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO sent your change to Slack but never got a clear answer back. The message, reaction, file or channel change may already be in Slack, so SMTO won't send it again on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Slack and look at the channel or thread you were changing. See whether the message, edit, reaction, file or channel change is already there. Slack may have made the change even though SMTO never got the confirmation.
  2. If you can't tell, ask the Agent only to read the latest messages in that channel or thread, and not to post or change anything yet. Reading the channel shows what really happened without making another change.
  3. Only if you're sure the change is missing, ask the Agent to make it once more. If it's already there, leave it. Sending it again without checking could post a duplicate message or repeat the change.

What success looks like

  • You've seen in Slack that the change appears exactly once, with no duplicate.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Slack connection. Don't keep repeating the request; each repeat could post again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Slack write (post, update, delete, reaction, channel change or file upload) was dispatched but not confirmed: a network failure, server error, malformed or mismatched acknowledgement, or failed read-only reconciliation left its outcome unknown.

What this means

  • Mutation transport, server errors, malformed acknowledgement, inconsistent upload identity or failed safe reconciliation leave the Slack write unconfirmed. The mutation may already have applied. A failed acknowledgement does not prove nonexecution; inspect exact IDs and retained correlations before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Mutation transport, server errors, malformed acknowledgement, inconsistent upload identity or failed safe reconciliation leave the Slack write unconfirmed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact channel/message, client_msg_id or file_id and retained request evidence.

How to fix it

  • Do not repeat the write. Using the original request's workspace_ref, channel_id, ts or thread_ts, plus any client_msg_id or stage reported in the error details, inspect actual Slack state with read-only operations (history, thread, message, reactions, file_info), and only issue a new write once the earlier one is confirmed absent.
  • Do not repeat the mutation. Inspect the exact channel/message, client_msg_id or file_id; reconcile provider state before any new action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and reconcile the earlier operation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Actual provider state is reconciled before any new write.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The mutation may already have applied. A failed acknowledgement does not prove nonexecution; inspect exact IDs and retained correlations before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
